name: Baa Atoll, Maldives
tagline: A private shore in a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve.
distinctive: Baa Atoll is a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve, known for its reefs and for the manta rays that gather at Hanifaru Bay in season. It is a place for doing very little, very well.

image.alt: A wooden jetty leading to overwater villas above a turquoise lagoon in the Maldives

moodNotes.sea: Your own stretch of lagoon, reef a few strokes from the steps, and nothing on the horizon.
moodNotes.lifetime: The seaplane landing alone is a memory, and the reef life of Baa Atoll is internationally recognised.
moodNotes.wellness: Barefoot days, spa rituals and uninterrupted sleep: restoration is the point.
moodNotes.weekend: The long flights from most departure points make a weekend impractical.

seasonNote: The northeast monsoon months, roughly December to April, are usually drier. The southwest monsoon brings more rain, and it is also the manta season in Baa Atoll.

arrival.transfer: Resorts arrange seaplane transfers from Malé, and seaplanes fly only in daylight. Some atolls are reached by domestic flight and speedboat instead.
arrival.groundNote: Late international arrivals may need a night near Malé before the seaplane. Confirm connection times with your resort.

driving.note: There are no roads between island resorts. The journey is by seaplane or boat.

transfer.label: Seaplane transfer
transfer.why: The flight low over the atolls is part of the arrival and takes you almost to your door.

stay.name: Soneva Fushi
stay.why: A barefoot-luxury island resort whose villas sit among the island's vegetation, suited to both couples and families.

watchWhy: A proper dive watch belongs on a reef holiday: a rotating bezel for snorkel time, and it needs no attention.
aromaWhy: Cool vetiver and a milky coconut note make an island villa smell quietly of the tropics without sweetness.

days.title: Land softly
days.text: Take the seaplane from Malé, then spend the rest of the day between the villa and the lagoon.

days.title: The house reef
days.text: Snorkel the reef with a guide in the morning. Rest through the heat, then take a boat out at sunset.

days.title: Rays and a sandbank
days.text: In season, ask about regulated visits to Hanifaru Bay for the mantas. Otherwise, take a picnic to a sandbank.

moreDays.title: A spa day
moreDays.text: Book a long treatment and hand the rest of the day to the hammock.

moreDays.title: Island life
moreDays.text: With the resort's guidance, visit a local island community respectfully.

moreDays.title: Night sky
moreDays.text: With little light pollution, the stars are extraordinary. Ask whether the resort has an observatory or a guided evening.
